title: The night the stars came back
text: A third of humanity can no longer see the Milky Way, because artificial light spills uselessly upwards {{1}} cities and dims the sky above them. Astronomers noticed first, {{2}} was only to be expected, but the ecological evidence is blunter: sky glow confuses migrating birds, draws insects to early deaths and blurs the seasons {{3}} plants. The night sky {{4}} doubled in brightness within living memory, and the loss is measured in more than poetry. Several national parks {{5}} now won dark-sky protection, {{6}} shielding is compulsory and lamps must aim away from the sky. {{7}} well as saving the stars, such rules save money, since light thrown sideways lights the pavement instead of the clouds. {{8}} takes only one clear night away from a city for the Milky Way to return, which may be why star-bathing trips are quietly becoming the new spa weekend.

gaps.explanation: The light originates from the cities: from.

gaps.hint: relative: noticed first, ___ was only to be expected
gaps.explanation: Sentential relative after the comma referring to the noticing.
Affected party takes 'for': the seasons for plants.

gaps.hint: auxiliary: the sky ___ doubled in brightness
gaps.explanation: Present perfect with a singular subject: has doubled.
Present perfect with a plural subject: have won.

gaps.hint: relative adverb: protection, ___ shielding is compulsory
gaps.explanation: 'Where' refers back to the protected parks as the place.

gaps.hint: preposition: ___ well as saving the stars
gaps.explanation: 'As well as' is the fixed additive phrase.

gaps.hint: dummy subject: ___ takes only one clear night
gaps.explanation: 'It takes X for Y' — the dummy subject of the cost phrase.
